title: Check: Crude Oil and Fractional Distillation (2)

questions.stem: As the chain length of hydrocarbons in crude oil increases, what happens to their viscosity and flammability?
questions.explanation: As chain length increases, viscosity increases because longer molecules tangle together more, making the liquid flow less easily. Flammability decreases because longer chains are harder to vaporise, requiring more energy to ignite. Short-chain fractions like petrol are runny and very flammable.

questions.stem: Why is crude oil described as a non-renewable resource?

options.text: It is too expensive to extract from the ground
It was formed over millions of years and is being used much faster than it can form
It can only be found in one country

questions.explanation: Crude oil formed over millions of years from the remains of ancient marine organisms under heat and pressure. We are using it far faster than it can be replaced naturally. Once used up, it cannot be reformed on any human timescale, making it a finite, non-renewable resource.
